title: PR #36990 added the support app's CourseTeamManageAPIView with only IsAuthenticated, without the support-role gate every sibling support view uses, so any learner can probe arbitrary accounts and instructors can read other users' course roles.

findings.explanation: The diff contains only serializer and URL routing code. All data access goes through Django ORM methods (model fields, context dict lookups). No raw SQL queries or string interpolation into SQL is present anywhere in the diff.

The test 'test_get_api_with_username_parameter' and 'test_get_api_with_user_id_parameter' show that a regular authenticated user (self.user) can query course team roles for *any* target user by supplying an arbitrary username or user_id query parameter. The test 'test_get_api_instructor_can_only_see_their_courses' suggests per-requester course scoping is implemented for instructors, but the GET endpoint appears to accept lookups by arbitrary user_id/username/email without verifying the requester is a support agent or admin. The actual view code is not included in the diff, so this is unconfirmed, but the test structure strongly suggests that ordinary authenticated users can enumerate other users' course roles (CWE-639/IDOR) and that any authenticated user can call the PUT role-assignment endpoint (CWE-862). The test 'test_put_api_missing_email_returns_400' logs in as self.user (a plain UserFactory user) and hits the PUT endpoint, receiving a 400 rather than a 401/403, which implies no authorization guard rejects unprivileged users on PUT.

evidence.content:
def test_get_api_with_username_parameter(self):
        """GET API: Can query by username parameter."""
        self.client.login(username=self.staff.username, password=TEST_PASSWORD)
        resp = self.client.get(self.url, {"username": self.user.username})
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertIsInstance(resp.data, list)

findings.suggested_fix: Ensure the GET endpoint requires the caller to be a support agent/admin (e.g., via IsAdminUser or a custom IsSupportStaff permission) before allowing lookups of arbitrary users' roles. The PUT endpoint should similarly require an explicit permission check (e.g., IsSupportStaff or IsAdminUser) and return 403 for unprivileged callers rather than proceeding to input validation. Regular instructors querying other users' roles should only be permitted for their own courses if that is the intended design, and this must be enforced server-side.
